title: Fractional Share Pools & Surge Smoothing Strategy for Dedicated Capacity (Q3 Roadmap)
creator: Leah Chen
description: Summary: Introduce a fractional-share allocation model for dedicated GPU pools combined with surge-smoothing policies to reduce overprovisioning and improve utilization predictability. The initiative will run as a mixed research-and-product program across Q3: design allocation primitives, prototype a scheduler that supports fractional shares (time-sliced or vGPU-like), validate surge-smoothing heuristics, and pilot with 2 high-usage customers on a canary pool. Goals: (1) Reduce committed-reservation waste by 18% on targeted pools, (2) Keep p95 latency regressions <5% under smoothing, (3) Demonstrate cost-per-token improvement >=12% for bursty workloads. Core deliverables: design spec for fractional share API, scheduler prototype, autoscale policy extension (smoothing window + hedging), canary rollout plan, observability dashboards and billing semantics. Success metrics/OKRs: OKR1: Capacity efficiency — M1: committed-to-utilization ratio +18% in targeted pools within 6 weeks of pilot; OKR2: Reliability — M2: maintain <=1% increase in error-rate during smoothing experiments; OKR3: Adoption — M3: onboard 2 paying customers to fractional pools and collect feedback. Non-goals: Not replacing Dedicated reserved SKUs; not addressing cross-region failover in initial phase.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fractional allocation could cause noisy neighbor latency spikes — Mitigation: conservative initial timeslices + QoS caps and KV-cache partitioning
Risk: Billing complexity for fractional usage — Mitigation: work with Finance to model per-second metering and expose clear invoices during pilot
Risk: Customers misunderstanding guarantees — Mitigation: dedicated docs, visible SLOs for fractional pools, opt-in only during beta
Risk: Scheduler changes destabilize other autoscale logic — Mitigation: feature flagging, canary branch, phased rollout, and rollback playbooks
